content:
This dispute centered on a husband’s attempt to claim co-ownership of a home built during the marriage on land that the wife had received as a pre-marital gift. The Court rejected the claim for division based on the principle of accession (Art. 934 CC), which dictates that the owner of the land automatically acquires ownership of any structure built upon it. Because the land was the wife's personal property acquired before the marriage, the house also became her exclusive asset, regardless of the marital regime. The non-owner spouse is not entitled to a property right but only to a credit right for the value of materials and labor contributed.
The case highlights the rigorous burden of proof placed on the claimant. The husband sought reimbursement for a furniture loan and construction materials, but the Court rejected the majority of these claims. Specifically, the claim regarding the furniture loan failed because the husband could not prove the installments were paid with personal funds rather than common family resources or wedding gifts. Similarly, claims for wedding gift division were dismissed due to a lack of specific evidence regarding their existence and value. Ultimately, the Court only awarded a partial credit of €7,613.00 for plumbing and marble expenses that were clearly verified through receipts and witness testimony.
